Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet

docs.takeaway: CLAUDE.md loads every session (target <200 lines); @imports; AGENTS.md is read only if imported when CLAUDE.md exists; auto memory toggle.
Skill frontmatter fields; names+descriptions always listed (desc+when_to_use capped at 1,536 chars); body loads on invoke and persists in context.
Hook events and JSON I/O: PreToolUse permissionDecision deny, Stop decision block + stop_hook_active, PreCompact stdout steers summary, SessionEnd 1.5s default timeout.
Practical hook recipes; hooks give deterministic control instead of relying on the model to choose.
Subagent frontmatter (name, description, tools, model, maxTurns, skills); separate context window; model aliases haiku/sonnet/opus.
Settings scopes and precedence (managed > local > project > user); where hooks and permissions live.
Rules evaluate deny -> ask -> allow; first match wins; Bash/Read/Edit pattern syntax.
claude -p with --output-format json returns result, usage, total_cost_usd, num_turns; --bare skips CLAUDE.md/skills/hooks.
Open Agent Skills format: name (lowercase-hyphen, <=64, matches dir), description <=1024, scripts/references/assets, progressive disclosure.
Be concise, set degrees of freedom, keep SKILL.md small, one-level-deep references, scripts for deterministic work, evaluation-driven development.

docs.title: Building effective agents
docs.takeaway: Prefer simple composable workflows (chains, routing, evaluator-optimizer) before autonomous agents.

docs.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
docs.takeaway: Context is a finite attention budget: smallest high-signal token set, just-in-time retrieval, compaction, structured notes, sub-agents.

docs.title: Equipping agents with Agent Skills
docs.note: Post retitled by publisher (was "Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills").
docs.takeaway: Skills = folders of instructions/scripts/resources loaded progressively; metadata first, body on relevance, files on demand.

docs.title: Writing effective tools for agents
docs.takeaway: Design tools for agents: few high-leverage tools, meaningful concise outputs, clear errors, evaluate tools with realistic tasks.

docs.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
docs.takeaway: Orchestrator + parallel subagents wins on breadth but costs ~15x tokens; subagents return condensed findings.

docs.takeaway: Give Claude a check to run, manage context aggressively, enforce non-negotiable rules with hooks, use subagents for investigation.

docs.why: Official statement of what loads always vs on demand (CLAUDE.md, skill descriptions, hooks), the fact Phase 2 is designed around.
